title: Billing-aware burst delegation & repayment protocol (PRD - WIP)
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes a Billing-aware Burst Delegation and Repayment Protocol for Dedicated pools. Goal: let tenants borrow short-lived compute (burst) beyond their committed capacity while ensuring predictable per-tenant economics, clear incentives to return borrowed capacity, and simple accounting that ties to existing billing and quotas.

Context / problem:
- Dedicated customers buy reserved capacity (commits) and expect isolation + predictable unit economics. But workloads spike and customers want on-demand burst.
- Current burst designs focus on availability and isolation semantics only. They lack integrated billing signals: tenants either get free burst (bad margin) or are flat-charged (surprises / poor fairness).
- We need a mechanism that: 1) enables controlled burst, 2) ties burst usage to billing and repayment semantics, 3) prevents persistent overuse (tenant unfairness), and 4) integrates with fallback and throttling logic.

High-level approach: billing-aware burst delegation:
- Burst tokens: a short-lived, metered currency minted by the control plane when a tenant requests burst. Tokens encode: amount (gpu-minutes), expiry window, repayment terms (immediate bill, deferred credit, or credit-with-repayment).
- Delegation tiers: 1) Prepaid burst (charged at extended rate immediately), 2) Credit-line burst (deferred charge with repayment windows), 3) Emergency soft-allow (no-charge emergency lane; logged and rate-limited).
- Smart repayment: if tenant exceeds commit over an epoch, repayment options kick in: automatic conversion to additional reserved capacity (one-off invoice), token-based charge at premium, or automatic throttling plus pro-rated credit reversal.

Product & UX:
- Console: burst toggle per-tenant with three behavioral modes (Disabled, Soft-credit, Prepaid). Show live burst balance, projected next invoice impact, and historical burst usage heatmap.
- API primitives: /burst/request (size, duration, mode), /burst/status, /burst/release, /billing/repay (accepts repayment plan). Responses include token id, effective rate, and SLA implications (latency SLO relaxation).
- Billing labels and events: every burst token mapped to billing line item with tags: tenant_id, commit_id, burst_tier, region, model_family. Helps downstream cost analytics.

Runtime & orchestration integration:
- Admission control consults burst token store before placement. Tokens may be reserved optimistically (fast path) or require synchronous authorization for large requests.
- Fallback behavior: when resources scarce, admission policy checks: (1) local reserved capacity, (2) prepaid burst tokens, (3) credit-line tokens, (4) emergency lane. Use tenant-priority with soft-fallback to hosted or lower-fidelity model variant.
- Telemetry: token lifecycle events (mint, consume, partial-release, expire), repayment events, conversion to reserved commit. Surface to Console and SLO dashboards.

Economic model & rates: rough initial pricing (placeholder to be validated with finance):
- Prepaid burst: 3x committed per-GPU-minute rate
- Credit-line burst: 2x committed rate billed at end of month unless repaid within X hours at 1.5x (early repayment discount)
- Emergency lane: free for first N minutes per quarter to avoid soft outages; logged and subject to manual review for abuse

Safety & fairness controls:
- Per-tenant burst ceiling (absolute and relative to commit).
- Cooldown windows after heavy burst usage (auto-reduced burst allowance).
- Abuse detection: spike pattern detection + manual flags.
- Global pool watermark: if aggregate burst usage exceeds safety threshold, temporarily disable credit-line tokens.

Operational runbook (short):
- Alert: burst borrowing > 40% aggregate across region for 10m -> ops-oncall review.
- Incident actions: 1) throttle credit-line tokens, 2) switch non-critical tenants to emergency lane limits, 3) communicate via status page if degradation expected.
- Billing disputes: generate per-token ledger export, link to requests and traces, provide a 7-day rollback window for credits.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Lab prototyping: implement token store + simple prepaid lane (2 months).
2) Canary: 10 customers electing prepaid mode (1 month). Observe billing events and ledger reconciliation.
3) Beta: add credit-line burst for select heavy customers with explicit consent + legal addendum (2 months).
4) GA: emergency lane + UI polishing + billing automation (Quarterly).

Open questions / risks (TODO):
- Legal acceptability of retroactive charges for credit-line overflow (need finance and legal signoff).
- UX clarity: how to present projected bill spikes without scaring customers (mockups needed).
- Accounting complexity: do we reuse existing billing pipeline or introduce a secondary ledger?
- Edge case: multi-tenant models where a single request consumes resources on behalf of another tenant — how to attribute burst?

Metrics to evaluate success:
- % of bursts that are prepaid vs credit-line vs emergency
- Burst revenue uplift vs marginal cost delta
- Incidence of repayment disputes per 1000 tokens
- Latency SLO impact when burst is active
- Customer satisfaction (NPS delta) for customers using burst lanes

Next steps / owners:
- Prototype: eng-serving-runtime (Diego) + infra billing integration (Marcus) — spike due 2024-11-22
- Mockups + copy: product-design (Priya) — initial UI by 2024-12-06
- Finance/legal consult: billing-policy review meeting scheduled 2024-11-12 (Ava)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally rough — we want feedback on the repayment semantics and whether we should support negative-balance automatic throttles vs forced convert-to-reserve flows. Please comment inline or add to JIRA-DED-4821.

Appendix (examples):
- Example token: {token_id: tkn-0123, tenant: acme-inc, amount: 180 gpu-min, expiry: 2024-12-10T15:00Z, tier: credit-line, rate: 2x, repayment_window_hours: 72} 
- Example flow: tenant requests 5x burst for 30m -> control plane mints credit-line tokens (if under ceiling) -> runtime consumes tokens and tags traces -> month-end invoice includes burst line items -> tenant pays or triggers repayment plan -> if unpaid after grace, automatically propose conversion to additional reserved capacity (opt-out).

-- end of draft --
